title: GitHub Releases stop at v0.6.0: cut v0.7.0..v0.11.0 from CHANGELOG, date the headings, and make promote-release create the release
description: Dispatched by opum-agent under OPAG-646 (opum-ai/opum-agent#1185), on an operator report that GitHub shows no quest release. Measured here 2026-09-27: tags run v0.6.0..v0.11.0, but the only GitHub Release is v0.6.0 (published 2026-09-11), so releases/latest reads v0.6.0. Nothing in scripts/ or .github/workflows/ creates a GitHub Release, so every release since 0.6.0 skipped the step. lore-cli has the same step as item 2 of the printed closing checklist in its publish-release.sh; here it becomes an executed step instead. CHANGELOG version headings carry no dates, while lore's do. v0.8.0 is tagged but was never published to npm (its content shipped in 0.9.0), so its release must say so. v0.6.1 (tagged, never published) and v0.6.2 (published) also have no release; they are outside this dispatch and are reported to opum-agent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A non-draft GitHub Release exists for each of v0.7.0, v0.7.1, v0.8.0, v0.9.0, v0.10.0 and v0.11.0, each body being that version's CHANGELOG.md section; v0.8.0's title and body state it was tagged and never published; gh api repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/releases/latest reads v0.11.0

Every CHANGELOG.md version heading from 0.5.0 carries a date taken from a record: the npm registry time field (UTC) for a published version, the tag for the unpublished 0.8.0, with the source stated in the file; no date is inferred

promote-release.mjs --promote, after latest is verified moved, creates the GitHub Release for v<version> from its CHANGELOG section and marks it latest, or confirms one already exists; a dry run only reports what it would do; --rollback does not touch releases; tests cover section extraction, create, already-exists and a failed create

implementationNotes:
Evidence 2026-09-27.
AC1: node scripts/github-release.mjs --create cut v0.7.0, v0.7.1, v0.8.0, v0.9.0 and v0.10.0 with --not-latest, then v0.11.0 as latest. It was dry-run first. API read-back: releases/latest = v0.11.0 "Quest CLI 0.11.0"; all six are draft=false and prerelease=false; v0.8.0 is titled "Quest CLI 0.8.0 (tagged, never published)" and its body opens by saying so; 6/6 bodies equal changelogSection() of CHANGELOG.md. Still 9 remote tags, and every peel is unchanged (2d5dd6b, 9258018, 9d91fc3, e8eeaf1, bf30c5c, eb1d9f4): --verify-tag created none.
AC2: dated headings 0.5.0..0.11.0. Each published version uses the UTC day of npm time[@opum-ai/quest][version] (0.5.0 09-08, 0.6.0 09-09, 0.6.2 09-14, 0.7.0 and 0.7.1 09-15, 0.9.0 09-19, 0.10.0 09-24, 0.11.0 09-27). 0.8.0 uses its v0.8.0 tagger date, 2026-09-17T23:30Z. The CHANGELOG intro states the source.
AC3: test/qcli398-github-release.test.ts (12 tests) covers extraction, create, already-exists and failed create, plus an unreadable state and a dry run that makes no write. Third measurement: dropping the heading anchor fails exactly the predicted 0.1.1/0.1.10 test, 11 green. The first fixture let that mutant survive, and it was fixed. bun run check exit 0 (791 pass); lore check exit 0. A dry run against the real ~/.quest-release/promotion-0.11.0.json reached the step and printed "release v0.11.0 exists; would mark it latest". NOT exercised live: the post-promote call in --promote. It runs the same ensureGitHubRelease that cut the six releases above, and its first real run is the next promotion. --rollback returns before the release code.
finalSummary: GitHub Releases stopped at v0.6.0 because no release step ever cut one. Backfilled v0.7.0..v0.11.0 from CHANGELOG sections; v0.11.0 is latest, and v0.8.0 is labelled tagged-never-published. Verified by API read-back: 6/6 bodies match, tags unmoved. Dated every CHANGELOG version heading from 0.5.0, from npm registry time, or the tag for the unpublished 0.8.0. promote-release.mjs --promote now cuts the release (scripts/github-release.mjs) once latest is verified, and refuses before any tag moves if the CHANGELOG section is missing. Tests cover it, with a mutation check, and the runbook documents it. The post-promote call first runs live at the next promotion. v0.6.1 and v0.6.2 still have no release; they were outside OPAG-646 and are reported to opum-agent.
